@graph.name: Italian Wedding Soup
@graph.description: This cozy Italian Wedding Soup recipe features tender and flavorful meatballs, vegetables, and pasta in a delicious chicken broth.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb. ground Italian sausage (hot, mild, or sweet, $3.92)
½ cup small pasta (I used pearled couscous, $0.41**)

itemListElement.text: Gather the ingredients for your meatballs. I find making the meatballs first helps this recipe go a bit faster! You can also form your meatballs a day in advance, or freeze them for easier use later on.
itemListElement.name: Gather and prep

itemListElement.text: Mix dry ingredients for meatballs; combine the breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan cheese, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Stir to combine.
itemListElement.name: Mix dry ingredients

itemListElement.text: Add the Italian sausage, breadcrumb mixture, and egg to a large bowl.
itemListElement.name: Add everything to bowl

itemListElement.text: Use your hands or a fork to mix them together until just combined.
itemListElement.name: Mix until combined

itemListElement.text: Divide and shape the mixture into 20 small meatballs, about 1 Tbsp each. Set the meatballs aside.
itemListElement.name: Divide and shape

itemListElement.text: Dice the onion, carrots, and celery, and mince the garlic.
itemListElement.name: Prep the veggies

itemListElement.text: Add the olive oil to a large soup pot and heat over medium. Add the diced vegetables, garlic, and Italian seasoning, cooking until the vegetables have softened, about 4 minutes.
itemListElement.name: Saute the veggies

itemListElement.text: Add the chicken broth to the soup, stir to combine, then place a lid on top and bring it up to a boil.
itemListElement.name: Add broth and boil

itemListElement.text: Once the soup is boiling, add the meatballs to the soup and continue to boil until the meatballs are cooked through (about 10 minutes).
itemListElement.name: Boil until cooked

itemListElement.text: (Optional) If you prefer browned meatballs, you can cook them in a skillet with a little olive oil first over medium heat until browned on the outside, then transfer to the boiling soup to finish cooking at this stage in the recipe.
itemListElement.name: Brown the meatballs

itemListElement.text: Add the tiny pasta to the boiling soup and continue to boil until the pasta is tender (about 6 minutes).
itemListElement.name: Cook the pasta

itemListElement.text: Finally, stir in the fresh spinach until wilted. Give the soup a taste and adjust the seasonings to your liking. Top with optional parsley, if using. Serve hot and enjoy!
itemListElement.name: Add spinach and serve

We made this soup for the second time this month last night! Here are some tips.

Brown the meatballs in the large Dutch oven that you’ll use to cook the soup. Set them aside on a plate while you cook the rest of the recipe.

If you are using better than bouillon, just add the bouillon paste with the Italian seasoning and mix it into the veggies like you would with tomato paste. Pour in the water after. It’ll be well incorporated. 

Cook the pasta separately if you plan to have leftovers. I just put a scoop of the pasta at the bottom of my bowl and top it with plenty of soup. This helps it prevent it from getting too soft when storing leftovers. To reheat, just combine the pasta and soup and microwave for 1.5, stir, and microwave for a minute more or until hot. :)

Also—we ran out of Parmesan the first time we made this, and we just made the meatballs without it. It turned out just fine.
This was really good! I used chicken sausage and veggie broth and it turned out great! I also browned the meatballs before and it added a ton of flavor. 5 out of 5!
